title: Four bands maximize sharp-break information over a tested CPV wavelength range under equal log-depth errors
abstract: We derive a four-band design for one simultaneous complex periodic variable dip. With fixed outer wavelengths of 0.788 and 2.09 micrometres, a sharp break in 1.05 to 1.60 micrometres, and equal independent log-depth errors, inner bands at the range edges maximize the information determinant for slope change and break location at every interior break. An exact Fieller confidence-set tool permits known error covariance and weak slope changes. Synthetic trials with 3% depth errors and a slope change of 0.88 give curvature power of 0.973 at 1.18 micrometres. The median 95% location-set span is 0.358 micrometres. A same-endpoint comparison design gives power 0.671 and span 0.550. Even log spacing loses location information near the range edges. Matrix checks, quadratic inversion and noise trials validate the calculations. This is an observing-method forecast, not a detection or a grain model. Bandpass effects, unequal errors, unknown calibration bias and smooth breaks require further work.
